predecessors.name: Maya city-states (Postclassic)
predecessors.text: the Lake Petén Itzá region, inside Cliopatria's Later Mayan City-States shape from 1450 to 1546

successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the Itza kingdom around Lake Petén Itzá, taken when 'Nojpetén fell to a Spanish assault on 13 March 1697'

ledger.x: 1441: the Itza, expelled from Mayapan, settle Lake Petén Itzá and build Nojpetén.
1695: Spanish troops hold ground on the northern edge of the Itza sphere.
13 March 1697: the fighting ends with the fall of Nojpetén ('resulted in the final defeat of the independent kingdoms of central Petén').
13 March 1697: Nojpetén falls and the last independent Maya kingdom ends.

wars.name: Mirones expedition against the Itza
wars.outcome: The Itza won: 'on 27 January 1624, an Itza war party led by AjKʼin Pʼol caught Mirones and his soldiers off guard'.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Petén
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: road building from Yucatán in 1695, missionary visits in 1696, and the assault on Nojpetén in March 1697 ended the last independent Maya kingdom.

certainty.note: The Itza sphere ('much of Petén and parts of Belize') is approximate throughout; only the island capital and the lake shore are firm.
